Recently, more and more users have reported that their Macs are experiencing the spinning rainbow wheel when running macOS 26.5, with some saying their trackpads become completely unresponsive for several seconds.

Activity Monitor usually shows three "culprits," and there now appears to be a reliable fix...

I mentioned this issue last month and guessed it might be related to Apple Intelligence's photo scanning feature. When checking Activity Monitor, you typically find that one, two, or three processes are consuming extremely high CPU resources.

Macworld's Michael Simon has also been plagued by this issue.

He tried various methods without success, and finally found one that works: deleting the ~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight folder. This of course means the Mac needs to rebuild its Spotlight index, but he said the problem hasn't returned after two weeks. My own usage time is less than a day so far, but the issue hasn't resurfaced either.

If you're willing to wait for Spotlight data to be rebuilt, here are the steps to delete the data:

  • Open a Finder window.
  • From the Go menu, choose "Go to Folder..."
  • Paste: ~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight
  • Press CMD-A to select all, then right-click on any item and choose "Move to Trash"
  • Right-click on the Trash and choose "Empty Trash"
  • Confirm when prompted

If you're experiencing the same issue, please let us know in the comments whether this method works for you too.
